An offended Thornton reacted by offering passive-aggressive, cryptic, and monosyllabic answers throughout the segment. When asked about the band's origins, Thornton claimed he didn't know how long they had been together and instead launched into a story about reading monster magazines as a child. 

The breaking point for Canadian listeners came when Ghomeshi asked about the enthusiasm of Canadian audiences. Thornton responded with a direct insult:

> *"Canadian audiences are very quiet,"* Thornton said. *"We’re used to playing in places where people throw things and yell and scream... It’s like mashed potatoes with no gravy."*

The interview immediately went viral, sparking widespread anger across Canadian social media, blogs, and news outlets, with many criticizing Thornton for behaving like a "diva" and disrespecting a respected national broadcaster.

---

### Hostile Reception in Toronto and Montreal

The full weight of the public backlash hit the band the following night at Toronto’s historic Massey Hall, where The Boxmasters were opening for Willie Nelson. 

The moment Thornton took the stage, the crowd erupted into loud, persistent booing. Audience members repeatedly taunted the frontman by screaming "Mashed potatoes!" and shouting "Where’s the gravy?" at the stage.

Thornton attempted to address the hostile crowd mid-set, offering a defensive clarification rather than an apology:

> *"I love Canada. I love Canadian people,"* Thornton told the jeering crowd. *"My comment about the mashed potatoes was aimed at a guy on the radio this morning, not you."*

The explanation failed to win over the audience. Reports from Montreal media indicated that local fans were preparing a similar, if not harsher, welcome for the band's scheduled gig at the Bell Centre, with calls on local radio stations to boycott or drown out the band's set.

---

### The Official Reason for Cancellation

On Friday, prior to their scheduled performance in London, Ontario, promoter tour reps announced that The Boxmasters were dropping off the Canadian leg of the tour immediately.

The official reason provided by the band’s management cited health issues within the touring party:

> *"The Boxmasters have decided to drop off the remaining Canadian dates on the Willie Nelson tour due to one band member and three crew members coming down with the flu,"* the band said in a brief statement posted to their website.

Despite the official statement citing "flu-like symptoms," industry insiders and fans largely viewed the cancellation as a face-saving measure to escape the overwhelming negative publicity and hostile concert environments awaiting them in Quebec and Western Canada. 

Willie Nelson continued the tour solo, performing to sold-out Canadian crowds—who reportedly greeted the country icon with raucous applause and no shortage of potato-themed signs. 

The Boxmasters rejoined Nelson’s tour once it returned to the United States later that month.
